Kennen or Erkennen? German A2 Recognition Exercises

Choose kennen for familiarity and erkennen for recognising or identifying. Practise German meaning and verb forms with translations and explained answers.

A2 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Understand the difference

Kennen describes familiarity with someone or something: Ich kenne den Ort. Erkennen can mean recognising, identifying or discerning: Ich erkenne ihn an der Stimme. Both verbs can refer to the same person, but kennen concerns familiarity and erkennen the act of identifying in a situation.

Common mistake to avoid

Ich kenne sie does not say that I successfully recognise her in every photograph. Use erkennen for the identification process specified here.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Pay attention to the exact article, verb position or ending described in the rule.

Worked example 1Ich kenne diesen Weg seit meiner Kindheit.I have known this path since childhood.
Worked example 2Am roten Rucksack erkenne ich meine Freundin sofort.I immediately recognise my friend by her red backpack.
Worked example 3Wir kennen die neue Nachbarin noch nicht.We do not know the new neighbour yet.
Worked example 4Auf dem dunklen Foto erkenne ich kaum etwas.I can hardly make anything out in the dark photograph.

Practice: choose the right word

Choose kennen for existing familiarity or erkennen for identifying in the stated situation. Conjugate the chosen verb. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. Ich ___ die Autorin persönlich. (be familiar with)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: kenne

Kenne states personal familiarity with the author.

Question 2. An deiner Stimme ___ ich dich sofort. (recognise)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: erkenne

Erkenne describes identifying the person by their voice.

Question 3. Wir ___ das Restaurant schon lange. (know through familiarity)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: kennen

Kennen describes a long-standing familiarity with the restaurant.

Question 4. Ohne Brille ___ sie die kleinen Buchstaben nicht. (make out)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: erkennt

Erkennt can mean discerning letters visually.

Revise it so it sticks

Return to this lesson tomorrow and complete the four gaps without looking at the rule. Then write two of your own sentences using today's pattern. Check whether the subject, case and verb position match the explanation.
